## Activity

During January 2023, Central Eye Clinic completed 149 captures as part of routine site activity. The recorded activity provides the basis for reviewing image quality and grading performance for the month. Capture activity should continue to be monitored through the usual operational reporting arrangements, with any recurring issues raised promptly so that they can be followed up and addressed.

## Image quality

There were 4 ungradable captures, giving an ungradable rate of 2.7 per cent. This remains an important quality measure because images that cannot be graded may require additional work and can delay review. The clinic lead asks that recurring camera issues are logged with the service desk. Consistent recording of these issues will support investigation of equipment or process factors affecting image quality and help identify whether further action is required.

## Grading

A total of 34 results were graded referable during January 2023. The median grading wait was 2. This measure should continue to be reviewed alongside activity and image quality, so that changes in workload, image usability, or grading timeliness can be identified. Overall, the report provides a monthly view of service delivery at Central Eye Clinic and highlights the importance of maintaining reliable capture processes and timely escalation of operational concerns.
